text:
Maya: Quick design thought — what if we move from static tenant slabs to an adaptive slab allocator that migrates memory between tenancy classes based on short-term hotset churn?

Kevin: idea: like a credit-based rebalancer? give mostly-unused tenants low-priority reclaim credits and move them to a cold slab, free up contiguous blocks for hot tenants.

Olga: want to call out correctness concerns — migration must preserve prefix atomicity and not violate current lease invariants. we can't have two nodes thinking they own same prefix while migration in flight.

Sam: +1 on atomicity. maybe do migration as a three-phase operation: reserve target space, copy with MVCC tag, then switch owner in single lease update. need a fast path for tiny prefixes though.

Li: operational questions — how do we avoid oscillation? hot <-> cold flip-flop for bursty tenants. need hysteresis and decay window.

Maya: agreed on hysteresis. proposal sketch: track a per-tenant score = recent_hit_rate * weight - eviction_pressure. if score stays above threshold for window T, grant growth tokens; below lower threshold, shrink.

Kevin: can we encode growth tokens as existing lease metadata so other components already understand them? less surface area.

Olga: careful: leases are our correctness anchor. embedding too much allocator semantics into lease metadata couples runtime modules. consider a small, versioned allocator API instead: AllocateSlab(tenant, bytes, intent_id). returns provisional token; final Commit/Abort via intent_id.

Sam: example pseudo for rebalance loop:
```
for tenant in active_tenants:
  sample = hit_rate(tenant, window)
  if sample > grow_thr: request = AllocateSlab(tenant, delta, intent)
  if request.ok: Commit(intent)  // atomic ownership switch
  elif sample < shrink_thr: MarkForEvict(tenant, delta)
```

Li: metrics we need: per-tenant slab_size, migration_count, median_copy_latency, lease-conflicts, and oscillation_rate. we should gate by a feature flag and run on a canary pool.

Maya: test plan: unit tests for API invariants, integration tests with simulated leader failovers, fuzz tests that inject delayed commits to catch split-brain windows. also perf test with a mix of 95th percentile bursty tenants.

Kevin: rollback plan? if migration fails, we must be able to revert to previous ownership deterministically. intent IDs + persistent journal entry should handle that. also add an invariant checker that runs periodically to reconcile slab ownership with lease table.

Olga: one more correctness note: prefix-level read-after-write must see pending migrations as either completed or not visible. i.e., a migrating key should be readable from its old owner until commit. avoid split reads.

Sam: implementation complexity: contiguous slab requirement helps compaction but makes allocation harder. alternative: allow non-contiguous segments and maintain a segment map per tenant — simpler migration but higher lookup overhead. tradeoff.

Li: ops: expose commands to forcibly pin tenant slab (emergency) and to simulate migration for canary tests. add alert when migration_count spikes above baseline.

Maya: decision runway: if we can define a minimal allocator API (Allocate/Commit/Abort/Query) + intent journal + hysteresis scoring, we can ship incremental: start with soft-growth tokens (no physical move), then implement actual migration. agrees?

Kevin: +1. would like to own the allocator API PR.

Olga: I'll write the invariants doc for lease+migration interactions.

Sam: I'll draft a compactness vs fragmentation comparison (contiguous vs segmented).

Li: I'll set up canary flags + metric dashboards.

CI-bot: build/allocator-service#128 queued for review by Kevin, Maya. tests: 22 passed, 3 flaky.

Maya: thanks all — will sync in the design meeting tomorrow to lock APIs and test plan. :thumbsup:
